alignments.note: מִתַּחַת → beneath fused (rule 30). Two prepositions with neither carrying content the other lacks: rule 23 heads such a compound on the governing morpheme standing first, as מֵעַל → from and מֵאֵת → of head on מִן; the English word 'beneath' does not choose the source head. Competing reading heads on תַּחַת as the sense-bearing morpheme.
'dried up' phrasal, headed on the verb (rule 44).

מִמַּעַל → above fused (rule 30). The adverb מַעַל is a lexical content morpheme the preposition lacks (as מַעְלָה → above heads on it under rule 32), so rule 23's first sentence heads here; competing reading treats it as a pair of particles and heads on מִן.
'cut off' phrasal, discontinuous around the subject (rule 25); margin 'wither' set aside (rule 38).

review_notes: Corrected only the source head of מִתַּחַת → beneath: rule 23 heads a compound of two prepositions on the first (מֵעַל, מֵאֵת precedent), not on the morpheme whose sense the English happens to carry. מִמַּעַל keeps its head on the adverb, which is a content morpheme; both competing readings are named in the notes.
